userStories.title: Web-facing thread facts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose ordered send refusal, the thread kill switch and validated runner backends through additive API response facts.

**Motivation** — The web also lacks three facts: the API's 409 body carries only translated text (no key), so the web cannot tell `threads.closing` (which it must retry) from any other refusal; the kill switch is invisible, so the web cannot hide New thread; and project members cannot read runners' `threadBackends`, so the web cannot offer a backend picker.

**Approach** — `GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id` answers `ChatThreadDetail`. `sendRefusal` is the first refusal of B1's ordered send checks 3-10 for the thread's current state (kill switch, archived, cost cap, paused budget, runner offline, runner below v4, closing, turn running) or null; it does not depend on the viewer (`threads.notCreator` stays a send-time 403). `POST /:id/archive` answers the same detail (it already returns `get`). Create, `PATCH /:id`, and list items keep the `ChatThreadRecord` shape. `GET /projects/:slug/threads` answers `{ items, threadsEnabled }`. `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/runners` records gain `threadBackends`. After the contract changes, `bun run generate` regenerates `openapi.json` and the CLI client (types only; no CLI command).

- `ThreadsService.get(projectId, id)` — Baseline: `Promise<ChatThreadRecord>`. Target: `Promise<ChatThreadDetail>` where `ChatThreadDetail = ChatThreadRecord & { sendRefusal: ThreadSendRefusal | null }` (in `chat-thread.domain.ts`). `messages()` keeps calling a lookup that does not compute the refusal.
- `ChatThreadRepository` — gains `sendRefusalOf(projectId: string, thread: ChatThreadRecord): Promise<ThreadSendRefusal | null>`, implemented in `PrismaChatThreadRepository` by calling the existing private `sendRefusalFor` with `{ id, status, runnerId, repoId, projectId, costUsd: new Prisma.Decimal(thread.costUsd), maxCostUsd: new Prisma.Decimal(thread.maxCostUsd) }` and the thread's current THREAD job (read without locks: `id`, `state`, `leaseEpoch`). It writes nothing.
- `ThreadsController` (`threads.controller.ts`) — `GET :id` documents `ThreadDetailDto`; `POST :id/archive` already answers `this.threads.get(...)`, so it carries `sendRefusal` too (`ThreadDetailDto`).
- `ThreadsService.list(...)` — Baseline: `Promise<{ items: ChatThreadRecord[] }>`. Target: `Promise<{ items: ChatThreadRecord[]; threadsEnabled: boolean }>`, `threadsEnabled` read from `fleetConfig.threadsEnabled` on every call.
- `RunnerSummaryDto` — Baseline fields: `id, name, os, arch, labels, enabled, online, profiles`. Target: plus `threadBackends: { native: string[]; acp: string[] }`, read from the stored `capabilities.threadBackends` when `protocolVersion >= THREAD_MIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and both arrays hold only strings; otherwise `{ native: [], acp: [] }`.
- `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/dto/thread.dto.ts` — gains `ThreadDetailDto` (`ThreadDto` plus `sendRefusal`, enum of the eight refusals, nullable) used by `GET /:id`'s `@ApiResponse`; `ThreadListDto` gains `threadsEnabled: boolean`.

**Scope** — In: service/domain/repository/DTO/controller changes, additive endpoint cases and facts integration tests, OpenAPI/CLI regeneration. Update runner-summary.dto.spec.ts's closed-world equality to add `threadBackends: { native: [], acp: [] }`; runner-views.integration.spec.ts and fleet-openapi.contract.spec.ts sorted summary property lists gain `threadBackends` after `profiles`, with all other fields and RepoCheckResultDto unchanged. Additive endpoint.e2e.spec.ts cases assert the detail refusal, list flag and project runner backends; existing cases unchanged. Out: browser client core (US-002), controller/composables (US-003), pages (US-004..US-007), per-viewer API refusal, refusal on create/PATCH/list items, CLI commands and database migrations. `sendRefusal` on list items, on create and on `PATCH /:id` responses; only `GET /:id` and `POST /:id/archive` carry it. A per-viewer refusal on the API (`threads.notCreator` stays a send-time 403); the web hides acting controls from non-creators itself.

**Interface** — `export type ThreadSendRefusal = 'disabled' | 'archived' | 'costCap' | 'budgetPaused' | 'runnerOffline' | 'runnerOutdated' | 'closing' | 'turnRunning';`
`export function sendRefusal(state: ThreadSendState): ThreadSendRefusal | null;`
`export const THREAD_MIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4`.
`ChatThreadDetail = ChatThreadRecord & { sendRefusal: ThreadSendRefusal | null }`
`sendRefusalOf(projectId: string, thread: ChatThreadRecord): Promise<ThreadSendRefusal | null>`

Acceptance integration setup: boot with `app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = true`, project `web`, member `dev` (DEVELOPER) who created thread T on fleet repo `web-app`, maxCostUsd 5 and costUsd 0, no runner pinned and no THREAD job, requests as dev unless stated. Restore config changes in finally/afterEach. Unit service tests use a fake repository; integration tests require real Postgres and KODA_DB_TESTS=1.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers 200 with sendRefusal null.
[integration] With app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = false, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers 200 with sendRefusal 'disabled'.
[integration] After T is archived, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers sendRefusal 'archived'.
[integration] With T's costUsd set to 5 (equal to maxCostUsd), GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers sendRefusal 'costCap'.
[integration] With a THREAD job of T in UPLOADING, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers sendRefusal 'closing'.
[integration] With a THREAD job of T in RUNNING at lease epoch 1 and a THREAD_CLOSE FleetCommand for it at epoch 1, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers sendRefusal 'closing'.
[integration] With a pending user message in T and its THREAD job RUNNING, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T answers sendRefusal 'turnRunning'.
[integration] With T's costUsd at 5, GET /api/projects/web/threads/T called by a VIEWER member answers sendRefusal 'costCap' (the refusal does not depend on the viewer).
[integration] With app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = false, GET /api/projects/web/threads answers 200 with threadsEnabled false.

[unit] ThreadsService.list over a fake repository answers { items, threadsEnabled } with threadsEnabled read from the config object at call time (changing the config between two calls changes the flag).
[unit] RunnerSummaryDto.from for a record with protocolVersion 4 and capabilities.threadBackends { native: ['m1', 'm2'], acp: [] } returns threadBackends { native: ['m1', 'm2'], acp: [] }.
[unit] RunnerSummaryDto.from for a record with protocolVersion 3 and the same stored threadBackends returns threadBackends { native: [], acp: [] }.
[unit] RunnerSummaryDto.from for a record with protocolVersion 4 whose capabilities.threadBackends.native is [1] (not strings) returns threadBackends { native: [], acp: [] }.

[integration] GET /api/projects/web/fleet/runners by dev lists a runner enrolled at protocol 4 with capabilities threadBackends { native: ['m1'], acp: [] } with threadBackends { native: ['m1'], acp: [] }.
[unit] The committed openapi.json (read as the fleet OpenAPI contract spec reads it) gives ThreadDetailDto a sendRefusal property and ThreadListDto a threadsEnabled property.

routing.reasoning: Additive DTO/read-method changes reuse the existing refusal evaluator and summary mapper without altering send transactions; member-visible facts and users-only route preservation retain the security override.

The other fields are unchanged.

userStories.title: Thread client core: types, view logic, event stream, SSE route
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add thread DTO mirrors, pure display transformations and a validated, recoverable per-thread content SSE client/proxy.

**Motivation** — The API and runner halves of phase B are merged, but no page reaches them, so threads cannot be used or live-checked and koda-wk stays undeployed (fleet design doc §9.62).

**Approach** — `lib/thread-types.ts` mirrors the DTOs: `ThreadDto` (with `session`, `pendingQuestion: { requestId; text; expiresAt } | null`, `activeJob`, `tokens: { input; output; cacheRead; cacheWrite } | null`), `ThreadDetailDto` (`sendRefusal`), `ChatMessageDto` (with `toolSummary: ToolSummaryEntry[] | null`, `errorReason`), `ToolSummaryEntry { callId: string; name: string; input: string; isError: boolean | null; preview: string; decidedBy: string | null }`, `ThreadSendRefusal`, `ThreadLiveEvent`, `ThreadBackend = { kind: 'native'; model?: string; effort?: string } | { kind: 'acp'; agent: 'claude' | 'codex'; model?: string; effort?: string }`, `ThreadSkillSource { sourceId; owner; repo; sha; skills: { name; dir; description }[] }` (`ThreadDto.skills` is `ThreadSkillSource[]`; the header shows the flattened skill names), `RunnerThreadBackends { native: string[]; acp: string[] }`, `SessionLabel`, `ComposerReason = ThreadSendRefusal | 'readOnly'`. `FleetRunnerSummary` (`lib/fleet-types.ts`) gains `threadBackends: RunnerThreadBackends` (US-005).

`lib/thread-view.ts` (pure, no Vue):

| Function | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `applyDelta(messages, messageId, text): ChatMessageDto[] | null` | a new array whose message `messageId` has `text` appended to `content`; null when no message has that id (the caller refetches) |
| `mergeMessages(current, incoming): ChatMessageDto[]` | union by `id`, `incoming` wins except that a message `streaming` on both sides keeps the longer `content` (an older in-flight GET never shortens streamed text), ascending `seq`; an optimistic entry (id `local:<clientMessageId>`) is dropped when `incoming` holds a message with its `clientMessageId`; optimistic entries sort after every real message |
| `refetchAfterSeq(messages): number` | `seq - 1` of the lowest-`seq` real message whose `status` is `pending` or `streaming`, else the highest real `seq`, else 0 |
| `isTurnRunning(messages): boolean` | a message (real or optimistic) has `status` `pending` or `streaming` |
| `sessionLabel(thread): SessionLabel` | `'starting'` when `activeJob.state` is QUEUED or ASSIGNED; `'closing'` when it is UPLOADING; `'live'` when it is RUNNING; else `'failed'` when `session.state` is `failed`; else `'closed'` when `session` is non-null; else `'none'` |
| `composerState(thread, messages, viewer: { userId; isCreator }): { canSend: boolean; reason: ComposerReason | null }` | `reason` = `'readOnly'` when not the creator; else `thread.sendRefusal` when set; else `'turnRunning'` when `isTurnRunning(messages)` (the API sends no `thread` event when a turn starts, so `sendRefusal` can lag); else null; `canSend` = `reason === null` |
| `toolChipState(entry, messageStatus): 'running' | 'ok' | 'error' | 'denied' | 'unfinished'` | `'denied'` when `decidedBy === 'profile'`; else, when `isError === null`, `'running'` if `messageStatus` is `streaming` and `'unfinished'` otherwise; else `'error'` when `isError`; else `'ok'` |
| `newClientMessageId(): string` | a fresh id matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/` |
| `costText(thread): string` | `` `${usd(costUsd)} / ${usd(maxCostUsd)}` `` |

`lib/thread-event-stream.ts`: `parseThreadLiveEvent(type, raw): ThreadLiveEvent | null` (JSON object with a string `id`, `threadId`, and the type's fields as strings; anything else null) and `createThreadEventStream(url, handlers, deps: ProjectEventStreamDeps): { close(): void }` with `ThreadEventHandlers { onDelta, onMessage, onQuestion, onThread, onResync, onLiveChange(live: boolean) }`. It listens for `delta`, `message`, `question`, `thread` and `ready`; drops an event whose `id` it has seen (window 200); calls `onLiveChange(true)` on `ready`; on a reconnect after an error calls `onResync` once the new connection opens; on a terminal failure (`readyState === EVENT_SOURCE_CLOSED`) calls `onLiveChange(false)` and recovers like `createProjectEventStream` (refresh auth, `backoffMs`, give up after `MAX_TERMINAL_FAILURES`). The Nitro route `server/api/projects/[slug]/threads/[id]/events.get.ts` mirrors the project events route, calling `openThreadLiveUpstream` (slug rule as today; thread id `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`; either invalid → 400 without calling upstream).

Integration note: the controller contract in US-003 requires live=false on any stream error, not only terminal failures; therefore signal false on transient errors too, while leaving native EventSource transient reconnect and terminal auth/backoff recovery unchanged. Malformed SSE event data is ignored. SSE refused or dropped (429, network, 401) marks live false and resyncs on reconnect; the 2000 ms in-flight polling fallback itself belongs to US-003. Preserve existing project/user proxy builders and forward cookie through openLiveUpstreamUrl, aborting upstream on browser response close and passing non-200 upstream status through.

**Scope** — In: new types/view/stream modules, nested Nitro SSE wrapper, two new live-proxy exports and associated unit tests using a local FakeEventSource. Out: Vue controller and composables (US-003), list/navigation (US-004), FleetRunnerSummary field and picker (US-005), transcript rendering (US-006), actions/E2E (US-007); no proxy-side JWT expiry/heartbeat checks. US-002 only: the Nitro route's JWT expiry close and heartbeat re-check are the API's (`createLiveStream`); the route adds none and has no acceptance criterion for them.

**Interface** — `ThreadLiveEvent = { id; threadId; at } & ({ type: 'delta'; messageId; text } | { type: 'message'; messageId } | { type: 'question'; requestId; text } | { type: 'thread' })`.
`buildThreadLiveUpstreamUrl(slug: string, threadId: string, apiInternalUrl: string): string | null`
`openThreadLiveUpstream(req: LiveProxyRequest & { threadId: string }): Promise<LiveProxyResult>` (an invalid slug or id → `{ kind: 'error', status: 400 }` without fetching; otherwise `openLiveUpstreamUrl`). Retain the existing LiveProxyResult body's error text. Use `EVENT_SOURCE_CLOSED = 2`, `MAX_TERMINAL_FAILURES = 5`, `backoffMs(attempt)` and `ProjectEventStreamDeps` from project-event-stream.ts.

All thread state the page shows comes from the API. The web derives display state (session label, composer state, tool chip state) in pure functions in `lib/thread-view.ts` and never re-implements the send checks: the composer's reason is `thread.sendRefusal`, plus the viewer-only case (not the creator). Thread money arrives as `Decimal.toString()` strings (`costUsd` `'0'`, `maxCostUsd` `'5'`, `'1.25'`; the API's `mapThread`) and is shown with `usd()` as received; the browser never sums or re-rounds it (web context A7).

[unit] openThreadLiveUpstream for slug web, thread id th1, cookie koda_token=x and an injected fetchImpl calls fetchImpl once with the URL buildThreadLiveUpstreamUrl('web', 'th1', apiInternalUrl) returns and the header cookie: koda_token=x.

[unit] mergeMessages of current [{ id: 'm1', seq: 1 }, { id: 'local:c2', clientMessageId: 'c2' }] with incoming [{ id: 'm2', seq: 2 }] returns ids in the order m1, m2, local:c2.

[unit] composerState(t, [], { userId: 'u2', isCreator: false }) with t.sendRefusal null returns { canSend: false, reason: 'readOnly' }.

[unit] composerState(t, [{ id: 'm1', seq: 1, role: 'assistant', status: 'streaming', content: '' }], { userId: 'u1', isCreator: true }) with t.sendRefusal null returns { canSend: false, reason: 'turnRunning' }.

[unit] parseThreadLiveEvent('delta', '{"id":"e1","threadId":"th1","at":"x","type":"delta","messageId":"m1","text":"hi"}') returns an event with messageId m1 and text hi.

userStories.title: Thread controller and composables
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement the testable reactive thread controller and Nuxt adapters for history, live updates, optimistic sending and actions.

**Motivation** — The API and runner halves of phase B are merged, but no page reaches them, so threads cannot be used or live-checked and koda-wk stays undeployed (fleet design doc §9.62).

**Approach** — `lib/thread-controller.ts`: `createThreadController(deps: ThreadControllerDeps)` holds the page's state and is what `useThread` wraps; deps are `{ api: { get, post, patch }, slug, threadId, openStream(handlers): () => void, setTimer, clearTimer, now(): number }`. It returns `ThreadController = { thread: Ref<ThreadDetailDto | null>; messages: Ref<ChatMessageDto[]>; live: Ref<boolean>; load; start; stop; send; stopTurn; endSession; answer; raiseCap; archive }` (Vue `ref`s created by the controller; `live` starts false and turns false on any stream error, not only a terminal one). Paths are built with `apiPath`; queries pass as `{ query: { afterSeq: '<n>', limit: '200' } }` with string values. Behaviour:

- `load()`: `GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id`, then `GET .../messages` from `afterSeq` 0 with `limit` 200, repeating from the last `seq` while a page returns 200 items (at most 50 pages); the result is merged with `mergeMessages`, so an optimistic message survives a reload.
- `start()`: `openStream`. `onDelta` → `applyDelta`, or `refreshMessages()` when it returns null. `onMessage` → `refreshMessages()`. `onQuestion` and `onThread` → reload the thread. `onResync` → `load()`. `onLiveChange` sets `live`.
- `refreshMessages()`: `GET .../messages?afterSeq=<refetchAfterSeq(messages)>&limit=200`, merged with `mergeMessages`.
- **Polling fallback:** while `live` is false and `isTurnRunning(messages)`, every 2000 ms `refreshMessages()` and reload the thread; it stops when either condition ends. `stop()` of the controller clears it and closes the stream.
- `send(text)`: appends an optimistic message (`id: local:<cid>`, `role: user`, `status: pending`, `clientMessageId: cid`), then `POST .../messages { text, clientMessageId: cid }`; on success merges the returned `message`. On an `ApiError` with `code` 409 it reloads the thread: when `thread.sendRefusal === 'closing'` and less than 15000 ms have passed since the first attempt it retries after 2000 ms with the same `cid`; otherwise it removes the optimistic message and resolves `{ ok: false, error }`. Any other error removes the optimistic message and resolves `{ ok: false, error }`.
- `stopTurn()`, `endSession()`, `answer(requestId, text)`, `raiseCap(maxCostUsd: number)`, `archive()`: `POST .../stop`, `POST .../end-session`, `POST .../answer { requestId, text }`, `PATCH /:id { maxCostUsd }`, `POST .../archive`; each reloads the thread on success and resolves `{ ok: false, error }` on failure (the page toasts `extractApiError(error)`).

`composables/useThread.ts`: `useThread(slug, threadId): ThreadController`, wrapping the controller with `useApi`, `useAuth().refresh` for the stream, browser timers and `EventSource` (`openStream` = `createThreadEventStream` over `apiPath\`/api/projects/${slug}/threads/${threadId}/events\``); on mount (client only) it calls `load()` then `start()`, on unmount `stop()`. `composables/useThreads.ts`: `useThreads(slug)` → `{ threads: Ref<ThreadDto[]>; threadsEnabled: Ref<boolean>; status: Ref<'ACTIVE' | 'ARCHIVED'>; load(status = 'ACTIVE'): Promise<void> }`, `GET /projects/:slug/threads` with `{ query: { status, size: '100' } }`.

**Scope** — In: new controller, useThread/useThreads and controller/composable tests; drive captured stream handlers and fake API/time rather than real fetch in unit tests. Out: transport parsing/reconnect/proxy implementation (US-002), list/navigation (US-004), creation (US-005), detail presentation (US-006), composer/action UI/toasts and E2E (US-007). US-003 only: a thread whose `pendingQuestion.expiresAt` has passed still shows the card until the API clears it. No local business-rule reimplementation or translated-409 parsing.

**Interface** — `createThreadController(deps: ThreadControllerDeps)`
`ThreadController = { thread: Ref<ThreadDetailDto | null>; messages: Ref<ChatMessageDto[]>; live: Ref<boolean>; load; start; stop; send; stopTurn; endSession; answer; raiseCap; archive }`
`useThread(slug, threadId): ThreadController`
`useThreads(slug)` → `{ threads: Ref<ThreadDto[]>; threadsEnabled: Ref<boolean>; status: Ref<'ACTIVE' | 'ARCHIVED'>; load(status = 'ACTIVE'): Promise<void> }`.

SEAM-1: detail.sendRefusal drives closing retry, never the 409 message string. SEAM-2: useThread passes createThreadEventStream as production openStream and controller tests invoke the supplied handlers. SEAM-3: downstream list/detail pages stub useThreads/useThread, never $fetch. Respect the elapsed 15000 ms retry boundary, bounded paging, overlapping message refresh, same-cid optimism and accepted commit/delta duplication race. The controller must not introduce authentication or permission rules; it injects the existing refresh callback for its stream adapter.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createThreadController load(), with a fake api.get answering the thread, a first messages page of 200 items and a second page of 3, ends holding 203 messages.
[unit] After start(), calling the onDelta handler that openStream received with { messageId: 'm2', text: 'x' } for a held message m2 appends x to m2 without any api.get call.

[unit] Calling onDelta for a messageId not held calls api.get for /projects/web/threads/th1/messages with options.query.afterSeq equal to String(refetchAfterSeq(heldMessages)), preserving the specified refetch cursor with string query values.
[unit] Calling onResync calls api.get for /projects/web/threads/th1/messages with options.query.afterSeq '0' (sequence zero encoded as a string).
[unit] With onLiveChange(false) called and a held streaming message, advancing the fake timer by 2000 ms calls api.get for the messages route once.

[unit] useThread('web', 'th1') mounted in a component with a stubbed global EventSource opens one EventSource at /api/projects/web/threads/th1/events (the production openStream is createThreadEventStream).
[unit] send('hi') holds a pending user message with id local:<cid> before api.post resolves.
[unit] send('hi') posts { text: 'hi', clientMessageId: <cid> } to /projects/web/threads/th1/messages, where <cid> is the optimistic message's clientMessageId.
[unit] When api.post resolves { message: { id: 'm9', seq: 9, clientMessageId: <cid> }, jobId: null }, the held messages contain m9 and no local: entry.
[unit] When api.post rejects with ApiError code 409 and the reloaded thread has sendRefusal: 'closing', the controller posts again with the same clientMessageId after the fake timer advances 2000 ms.
[unit] When every reload answers sendRefusal: 'closing' and the fake clock passes 15000 ms since the first attempt, send resolves { ok: false } with no local: message held.
[unit] When api.post rejects with ApiError code 409 and the reloaded thread has sendRefusal: 'turnRunning', send resolves { ok: false } after exactly one post.
[unit] answer('q1', 'yes') posts { requestId: 'q1', text: 'yes' } to /projects/web/threads/th1/answer.
[unit] raiseCap(8) patches /projects/web/threads/th1 with { maxCostUsd: 8 }.
[unit] useThreads('web') with a stubbed $api.get resolving { items: [t], threadsEnabled: false } exposes threadsEnabled false after load().

routing.reasoning: New reactive controller coordinates paging, SSE/refetch races, optimistic deduplication, retry deadlines and polling; useAuth refresh integration and thread session actions trigger the security override.

userStories.title: Thread list page and navigation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make project threads discoverable through navigation, breadcrumbs and an Active/Archived list with role- and kill-switch-gated creation.

**Motivation** — The API and runner halves of phase B are merged, but no page reaches them, so threads cannot be used or live-checked and koda-wk stays undeployed (fleet design doc §9.62).

**Approach** — **Navigation:** sidebar WORK section link `/:project/threads` (`nav.threads`, icon `MessagesSquare`) after Agents; palette entry `threads`; breadcrumbs `Koda / <project> / Threads` and, below it, `Threads` linked plus `fleet.threads.new.title` or the thread page leaf `fleet.threads.detail.title`.

**`/:project/threads`:** Active | Archived switch (`status` query of the list route); rows: title (link), creator (`nameOf(createdById)`, else the id), `feat/<feature>`, backend label, session label, last activity, `costText`; New thread button (`fleet.threads.list.newThread`) shown only when `canWorkOnFleet(role)` and `threadsEnabled`; an empty state per status.

- `apps/web/layouts/default.vue` — the project WORK section gains a Threads link after Agents; `breadcrumbItems` gains thread paths.
- `apps/web/components/CommandPalette.vue` — the project entries gain `threads` after `project-agents`.

Component contract:
| Component | Props | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| `ThreadListTable` | `threads: ThreadDto[]`, `status`, `nameOf(userId): string | null`, `slug` | — |

`composables/useThreads.ts`: `useThreads(slug)` → `{ threads: Ref<ThreadDto[]>; threadsEnabled: Ref<boolean>; status: Ref<'ACTIVE' | 'ARCHIVED'>; load(status = 'ACTIVE'): Promise<void> }`, `GET /projects/:slug/threads` with `{ query: { status, size: '100' } }`.

`apps/web/composables/useProjectViewerRole.ts` — `useProjectViewerRole(slug)` → the `useAsyncData` result; its `data.value` is `{ canManage, viewerRole }`, the argument `canWorkOnFleet` takes.

**Goal** — Display the live thread header/transcript, tool chips and pending question safely, with a running-turn tab-title indicator.

**Motivation** — The API and runner halves of phase B are merged, but no page reaches them, so threads cannot be used or live-checked and koda-wk stays undeployed (fleet design doc §9.62).

**Approach** — **`/:project/threads/:id`:** `ThreadHeader` (title, `feat/<feature>`, backend label, runner name and online dot from the project runner summaries, skill names, `costText`, `tokenText(input + output)`, session label); `ThreadTimeline` of `ThreadMessage` (assistant: `renderThreadMarkdown(content)`; user: plain text; a streaming indicator while `status === 'streaming'`; an end marker for `errored`, `cancelled`, `timed_out` and `interrupted` (`fleet.threads.detail.status.<status>`) with `errorReason` as plain text; tool chips), a context-reset marker when `session.contextReset`, and `ThreadQuestionCard` for `pendingQuestion`. `useHead` title: the thread title, prefixed `• ` while `isTurnRunning(messages)`.

**B4-D1:** assistant message `content` renders as sanitized Markdown through `renderMarkdownOrEscape` (umbrella §6.1). Everything else a runner or agent wrote renders through `{{ }}` interpolation only, never `v-html`: user messages, `errorReason`, tool `name` / `input` / `preview`, question text and `session.reason`. US-006 updates the web context's "never `v-html`" line to name this one exception.

**B4-D2:** all thread state the page shows comes from the API. The web derives display state (session label, composer state, tool chip state) in pure functions in `lib/thread-view.ts` and never re-implements the send checks: the composer's reason is `thread.sendRefusal`, plus the viewer-only case (not the creator).

**B4-D3:** thread money arrives as `Decimal.toString()` strings (`costUsd` `'0'`, `maxCostUsd` `'5'`, `'1.25'`; the API's `mapThread`) and is shown with `usd()` as received; the browser never sums or re-rounds it (web context A7).

**B4-D6:** thread Markdown shows no remote images. `renderThreadMarkdown(content)` (`lib/thread-markdown.ts`, US-006) renders through `renderMarkdownOrEscape` and then removes every `img` element, so agent-steered text (repo content, prompt injection) cannot make the browser fetch a URL. Links stay (they need a click).

userStories.title: Composer, session controls and the E2E journey
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete creator messaging/question/session actions and manager archive UI, and exercise the live browser workflow against a v4 ScriptedRunner.

**Motivation** — The API and runner halves of phase B are merged, but no page reaches them, so threads cannot be used or live-checked and koda-wk stays undeployed (fleet design doc §9.62).

**Approach** — **Composer and controls (US-007):** the composer and the answer input validate with vee-validate + a zod schema (trimmed text, non-empty, at most 32768 UTF-8 bytes, the API's limit). `ThreadComposer` for the creator: a textarea where Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline; Send disabled with the reason text `fleet.threads.refusal.<reason>` when `composerState` refuses; Stop shown while `isTurnRunning`. Non-creators see `fleet.threads.composer.readOnly` instead. `ThreadControls`: End session (creator, `sessionLabel === 'live'`), Raise cap (creator, a dialog with the same cap rule), Archive (creator or `canManage`, confirm dialog; hidden when archived). `ThreadQuestionCard` shows an answer input and Send to the creator only.

Component contracts (props / emits) the pages bind:
| Component | Props | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| `ThreadComposer` | `composerState`, `turnRunning: boolean` | `send(text)`, `stop` |
| `ThreadControls` | `isCreator: boolean`, `canManage: boolean`, `sessionLabel`, `archived: boolean` | `endSession`, `raiseCap(value: number)`, `archive` |
| `ThreadQuestionCard` | `question: { requestId; text; expiresAt }`, `isCreator: boolean` | `answer(requestId, text)` |

The thread page binds each emit to the matching `useThread()` method and toasts `extractApiError(error)` for every `{ ok: false, error }`. Stop / end session / answer / cap / archive fails: toast `extractApiError(error)`; state reloaded on the next event. Kill switch off: New thread hidden; `sendRefusal 'disabled'` shown in the composer. Composer reason comes from thread-view, not a copied server send rule. Cap validation is 0.0001..10000 with at most four decimals, emitting a number. Complete the already-created question card and its ThreadTimeline answer forwarding, then bind send/stop/endSession/raiseCap/archive/answer at the detail page. A noncreator project manager gets Archive only, not other creator actions.

### E2E journey (US-007)

`tests/e2e/fleet-threads.e2e.spec.ts` (B4-R2), against the e2e API started with `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED: 'true'`: `ScriptedRunner.enroll(adminToken, name, { threads: true, threadModel })` enrolls at protocol 4 (the `threads` branch of `protocolVersion` wins over `logs` and `relay`) with the default e2e capabilities plus `threadBackends: { native: [threadModel], acp: [] }`, and heartbeats. `threadModel` is unique per run (`e2e-model-<suffix>`) so no other scripted runner of the suite matches the THREAD job. `SyncCommand['type']` gains the five thread command types. The admin (a project member of the seeded fleet project) opens `/<project>/threads/new`, creates a thread on the seeded repo with model `threadModel`, and sends `hello` from the thread page. The test reads the job id from `GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id` (`activeJob.id`) and the user message id from `GET .../messages`; the runner takes the THREAD job's ASSIGN (`acceptAssign(jobId)`), reports `RUNNING`, and uploads `thread` lines with `putLog(lease, 'thread', ...)`: `session_started { resumed: false }`, `input_consumed { messageId }`, `turn_start { turnId: 't1' }`, `text_delta { turnId: 't1', round: 0, text: 'Hello from the runner' }`. The page shows `Hello from the runner` without a reload and a Stop button; clicking Stop delivers a `THREAD_STOP_TURN` command to the runner (`takeCommand`). The runner then uploads `turn_end` (`status: 'cancelled'`, `output: ''`, zero usage and cost). A second user, created with `createUser` and added as a VIEWER with `addProjectMember`, opens the same thread, sees `Hello from the runner`, and sees `fleet.threads.composer.readOnly` instead of a textarea. Verified with `bun run test:e2e -- fleet-threads` in `apps/web`; Playwright specs are not nax acceptance criteria.

One Playwright journey against a protocol-v4 `ScriptedRunner` (create, send, live reply, Stop, read-only second member). Closing retry and question cards are covered by Jest. Extend ScriptedRunner.enroll opts.threads and opts.threadModel, putLog's stream union with 'thread', and SyncCommand['type'] with THREAD_INPUT, THREAD_ANSWER, THREAD_STOP_TURN, THREAD_CLOSE, THREAD_PUBLISH. Preserve existing logs/relay/configJobs behavior when threads is not requested. Add FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED: 'true' to playwright.config.ts API webServer env. Use waitForHydration, never networkidle. Add fleet.threads.composer.*, fleet.threads.refusal.* (eight ThreadSendRefusal values plus readOnly), fleet.threads.controls.* to both locales, preserving existing keys; no | or @ in fleet messages.

**Scope** — In: composer/controls, creator question-answer validation in the existing question card, detail-page event bindings/toasts, action locales and component/controller verification plus one scripted-v4 Playwright journey. Out: API authority (US-001), stream/controller behavior (US-002/US-003), list (US-004), creation implementation (US-005), transcript rendering (US-006); phase-C publish/plan/run actions despite exposing THREAD_PUBLISH in the test fixture union. Publish, Plan, Run, the action bar, "Discard unpublished changes", commit markers and PLAN/RUN job cards belong to phase C. US-007 only: the E2E journey covers create, send, live reply, Stop and a read-only member; closing retry, question answer, context reset and archive are covered by component and controller tests only.
